title: Art Through Time
subtitle: Six periods, six questions somebody was trying to answer.
objectives: Order the main periods of art history
Say what question each period was answering

cards.title: Every period was solving a problem
cards.text: Art history taught as a list of styles is a list to forget. Taught as a series of questions, each style is the answer somebody found.

cards.title: Six questions, six periods
points: **Prehistoric:** can I record that this happened?
**Classical:** can I make the body ideal?
**Realism:** can I paint exactly what the eye sees?
**Modernism:** why should art look like anything at all?

cards.title: Six buttons
cards.text: Tap each period. The second line is the Philippine example.

question.explain: The oldest known artwork in the Philippines, in Rizal.

cards.title: Who did what, and when
cards.text: These three come up every year.
points: **Juan Luna:** the *Spoliarium*, 1884. Gold medal in Madrid.
**Fernando Amorsolo:** sunlit rural scenes; first National Artist.
**Victorio Edades:** broke with that style in the 1920s.
**Carlos "Botong" Francisco:** the great muralist of history.

cards.title: Concept art is the newest academic realism
cards.text: Before anything is built in a game, somebody paints it.
points: **Concept art decides** the shape of a world.
**It is painted to be believed**, not to be pretty.
**Same discipline as realism:** light, weight, material.
**Then modellers build** from the painting.

question.explain: 1884, and it won gold at the Madrid exposition.

cards.title: A car body is sculpture with rules
cards.text: Designers draw it, then physics edits it.
points: **The line has to look fast** standing still.
**And it has to let air past** without dragging.
**Clay models are still carved by hand** at full size.
**Art under constraint** is still art.

cards.title: Art is evidence
cards.text: Most of what we know about daily life before writing came from pictures.
points: **What they wore. What they hunted. What they feared.**
**None of that was written** at Angono.
**The carvings are the record.**
**Ask of any artwork:** what does this prove happened?

terms.def: Painting a subject as the eye would see it.
A painting made directly on a wall.

cards.title: The tools, not the pictures
cards.alt: Raw ochre pigment and a stone tool, a bristle brush with oil paints, and a stylus on a graphics tablet
cards.text: Ochre and a stone, a brush and oil paint, a stylus. The question changed and so did these.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Each period answers a question: record, idealise, copy, or break.
Angono: 127 carvings, about 3000 BC, the oldest art here.
Luna painted the Spoliarium; Amorsolo painted sunlight; Edades broke away.
Art is evidence of what happened, not only decoration.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 4 MAPEH, Arts strand. Periods are given as questions rather than labels, because the question explains the look and a label does not. Each period carries a Philippine example in the same row as the European one, so the local material is not a bolted-on section. Angono is the anchor for the earliest period and is specific — 127 figures, about 3000 BC, in Rizal. The three painters who appear in every Grade 6 paper get their own card with the one fact each that is actually asked. The closing lens makes the transferable point: art is evidence, and the right question to ask of an artwork is what it proves happened.
discussion: Ask what question each period was answering.
Ask which painter did which work.
Ask what the Angono carvings prove about the people who made them.
Ask what constraints a car designer works under.
extension: Have him draw the same object realistically, then stylised, then abstract.
Have him find concept art for a game he plays and describe the light in it.
misconceptions: "Older art is worse art." Each period solved a different problem.
"Art is decoration." It is often the only surviving record.
